title: Transform with map
description: Using Array#map, build a new array with every element doubled.
hint: map yields each element to the block and collects the block's return values: arr.map { |x| x * 2 }

payload.prompt: Using Array#map, build a new array with every element doubled.

approaches.note: map yields each element to the block and collects the return values into a NEW array — the original stays untouched.
collect is map's exact alias; most Ruby code says map.

title: Filter with select
description: Using Array#select, keep only the even numbers.
hint: The &:method shorthand turns a symbol into a block: arr.select(&:even?)

payload.prompt: Using Array#select, keep only the even numbers.

approaches.note: &:even? is Symbol#to_proc — it expands to { |x| x.even? }. The idiomatic filter.
Same filter with an explicit block. Predicate methods ending in ? read like questions: 'is x even?'
The arithmetic way — works in any language, but even? states the intent directly and can't get the comparison backwards.

title: Safe nested lookup with dig
description: Using Hash#dig, read the nested value at :user, then :name — returning nil instead of raising when a key is missing.
hint: dig takes one key per nesting level: h.dig(:user, :name)

payload.prompt: Using Hash#dig, read the nested value at :user, then :name.

approaches.note: dig walks one key per nesting level and returns nil at the FIRST missing key instead of raising NoMethodError.
The hand-guarded chain dig replaces — every level needs its own nil check, which is exactly the noise dig removes.

title: Sum it all up
description: Sum every element of the array — any idiomatic way counts.
hint: reduce(:+) folds the array through +; Array#sum and inject(:+) say the same thing

payload.prompt: Sum every element of the array.

approaches.note: The direct method — says exactly what it does. Reach for it first when you really are summing.
reduce folds the array through an operator; the symbol form hands + straight to the fold.
The explicit fold reduce(:+) expands to: acc starts at 0 and accumulates every element. inject and reduce are aliases.

title: Shout every name
description: Using map with the &:symbol shorthand, upcase every name in the array.

payload.prompt: Using map with the &:symbol shorthand, upcase every name.

approaches.note: &:upcase expands to { |name| name.upcase } — map + Symbol#to_proc is the standard one-call transform.
The same transform with an explicit block — needed as soon as the block does more than one call.
